actions.review: The official v7.0.1 manifest declares Node 24. The event ref and SHA still select the PR merge or the dispatched branch commit, and full history retains the exact-ref fallback. Both workflows still disable persisted credentials. The runner-temporary credential change and the v7 unsafe fork checkout restriction require no new input for these event types.

The official v7.1.0 manifest declares Node 24 and installs the requested Node 24 toolchain before restoring the explicit pnpm store cache. Cache identity still uses platform, architecture, package manager and the pnpm-lock.yaml hash. Automatic npm cache detection is bypassed by the explicit cache input. The ESM migration and removal of the dummy npm auth token do not affect this workflow, which omits registry configuration.

The immutable release runs Node 24 on hosted Ubuntu and Windows. The setup and successful post bundles retain the exact uv version-file, Python 3.12, supplied Linux and Windows archive checksums, GitHub Releases download and existing cache settings. The new optional require-checksums input defaults to false, preserving the existing tool-cache behavior and explicit checksum validation on download. The optional Windows Python junction repair is for cache-python; this workflow leaves that input disabled. The bundled runtime dependency undici moves from 8.10.0 to 8.11.0 under MIT. Workflow permissions remain contents:read.

The official v6.1.1 manifest declares Node 24. The v6 bootstrap supports pnpm 11 and selects the exact packageManager version from the root package.json, exposing its executable before setup-node reads the store path. The default disables its own cache and dependency installation, leaving setup-node's explicit cache and the frozen workflow install in charge.

Official upstream commit and action manifest inspected. Existing setup/cache/artifact role retained; contents:read only, no product secrets or third-party composite action calls. Native and Linux CI required after change.

The reviewed v6.1.0 restore entrypoint runs the official Node 24 restore-only bundle. It returns the resolved primary key and a matched key on restoration. Selected checks that use neither workspace build outputs nor Chromium start with their normal pinned tools. Other tasks can read the complete archive.

The reviewed v6.1.0 save entrypoint runs the official Node 24 save-only bundle. A successful full job can save the existing Cargo paths under the resolved primary key after a miss or fallback. A selected task cannot publish an incomplete target under the full key.

The official v8.0.2 manifest declares Node 24 and fails on artifact digest mismatch by default. It reads artifacts from the current workflow run with its Actions runtime access. The protected job requests only current-attempt Windows artifacts, uses separate directories and verifies checkout, selection and raw check log digests before publishing the combined report.

The official v7.0.2 manifest declares Node 24. The new direct-file mode requires archive: false. The default ZIP path preserves the named verification and timing archives, including their existing paths, hidden-file handling, missing-file failure, retention, and artifact ID and digest outputs.

advisory_dispositions.name: glib
advisory_dispositions.reason: Upstream reports unsound VariantStrIter behavior below 0.20.0; upgrading that GTK family independently is not compatible with the current Tauri graph. Both dependencies occur only in the unsupported GTK desktop graph. Current Windows workspace and all-target portable crates exclude them. Scope is rechecked on every online review; revisit before adding Linux desktop support or by expiry.

advisory_dispositions.name: proc-macro-error
advisory_dispositions.reason: Upstream reports the macro helper as unmaintained with no patched version. Both dependencies occur only in the unsupported GTK desktop graph. Current Windows workspace and all-target portable crates exclude them. Scope is rechecked on every online review; revisit before adding Linux desktop support or by expiry.

advisory_dispositions.name: block-buffer
advisory_dispositions.reason: OSV currently starts at zero, while the publisher primary advisory explicitly affects >=0.11.0,<0.12.1. Locked 0.10.4 is outside that primary range. Every online review fetches and verifies the exact primary identity and reviewed range; changed/unavailable metadata fails. This is an exact version discrepancy disposition, not a broad severity waiver.

advisory_dispositions.name: chrono
advisory_dispositions.reason: RustSec reports that chrono is unmaintained. Cargo.lock includes this optional dependency of serde_with. Each online review checks its absence from the Windows desktop graph and all targets of the portable crates. Reassess on a graph change or expiry.

advisory_dispositions.name: picomatch
advisory_dispositions.reason: The build-tool patch rejects both repeating extglob operators during parsing. Every online review checks the locked patch and the actual matchers loaded by Vite, tinyglobby and fdir. A new upstream release or expiry requires review and replacement when a suitable fix is available.

license_review.scope: All locked development and target packages. Declarations are retained from exact upstream metadata, not a claim that every dependency is shipped.
notice_obligations: Retain original copyright and license texts for MIT, BSD, ISC, Zlib, PSF, Unicode and other included packages.
Preserve required Apache NOTICE and attribution; satisfy each conjunctive license obligation and record a chosen permitted branch for alternative licenses when packaging.
For MPL-covered files in fqdn/pathspec and Mozilla-derived Rust dependencies, retain notices and provide covered source as required when distributed. No covered files are modified in M0.
release-artifacts remains blocked until actual installer contents, bundled notice texts and any source obligations are verified. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES is an inventory aid, not that acceptance.
license_review.format_dependency: Replaced jsonschema[format] with upstream format-nongpl at the same locked jsonschema version to remove the unnecessary GPL-only rfc3987 dependency while retaining schema format validation.

maintenance.owner: Repository implementation agent, with owner review for product/permission/boundary decisions.
maintenance.automation: Weekly bounded Dependabot proposals for GitHub Actions and Cargo activate when .github/dependabot.yml reaches the default branch. No auto-merge.
maintenance.manual_ecosystems: Reviewed on 2026-11-21. GitHub.com supports pnpm 11 through the npm ecosystem. The hosted matrix lists uv 0.11, while released Dependabot Core 0.405.0 uses uv 0.13.7 internally. ScopeHub requires exact uv 0.13.9. Use the pinned native package managers for this repository's Python and npm maintenance. Enable npm proposals only in a reviewed updater configuration that verifies the frozen pnpm lock, local patch and license inventory. Revisit hosted uv automation when the updater resolves the exact project pin and a trial proves it can update the locked graph.
procedure: On the next active development session, inspect the due date and open a maintenance task when due; newly reported relevant advisories trigger earlier review.

Review the open Dependabot queue and each recorded proposal by exact head and hosted run. Reconcile changed heads against the current graph, record shipped replacements after integration, and retain closed or superseded decisions with their original evidence. Reopen review when a deferred trigger is met or a replacement disappears from the supported graph.

Check release notes and concrete benefit. Update one coherent dependency family, regenerate locks with the pinned manager, refresh the inventory and inspect its diff. Never automatically approve newly encountered licenses or advisories.

Actions: resolve the reviewed upstream release to its official full commit and inspect each used manifest, runtime declaration, runner support, release notes, implementation, inputs and permissions. Check hosted job logs and annotations for forced runtime or deprecation warnings, then retain matching source and artifact identities for changed verification workflows.

At integrated pull request or branch retirement, or when cache pressure is observed, list GitHub Actions cache IDs, refs and sizes. Preserve default and active scopes and any caches needed by pending reruns. Once evidence is retained, manually retire only rebuildable entries scoped solely to a verified closed pull request or retired head. Main cannot restore archives scoped to a closed pull request's merge ref. Keep inventory read-only and use existing operator authorization for retirement.

Python/npm: inspect upstream releases; use uv lock --upgrade-package <name> or pnpm update <name> within the intended range. For Cargo use cargo update -p <name>. Major upgrades need an explicit compatibility plan.
Toolchains: review Python 3.12, Node 24, pinned pnpm, Rust and uv together with doctor expectations, workflow setup, locks and native build compatibility.

Run fast/affected checks, fresh dependency-review and Linux/Windows integration. Retain failures, source checkpoints and matching reports. Keep packaging/soak checks at their declared cadence unless the change needs them.

related_toolchain_finding.observation: The separately pinned uv 0.12.24 binary is affected when using its default bundled CA roots. The setup-uv Action update does not change the uv binary or remediate its trust store. The package inventory scan does not cover the installed uv executable.
related_toolchain_finding.revisit: Review a patched uv toolchain at or above 0.13.4 before the 2026-11-28 maintenance deadline or immediately if the existing download trust cannot be established. Verify the exact uv release checksum, lock compatibility, Python 3.12 setup and Linux/Windows verification before changing the separate tool pin.

uv_toolchain_review.review: Both original archives matched their publisher SHA-256, Astral manifest and GitHub release metadata. GitHub Artifact Attestations verified both files against astral-sh/uv's release workflow. 0.13.9 retains the CA bundle correction from 0.13.4 and the intermediate key distrust and managed Python refresh from 0.13.5. It also improves equivalent platform marker checks and rejects wheels advertised under another package name. The local Python 3.12 trial passed uv lock --check and uv sync --locked with the existing byte-identical lock.
